text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Maltese foreign ministry says the United States had refused to reconsider a unilateral decision to end an income tax treaty. The decision means some 400 Maltese residents who receive American social benefits, having once worked in the United States, will be liable to a 5.5 percent withholding tax. The agreement, which ends on January 1, also includes provisions on the avoidance of double taxation. The United States said the decision to terminate the agreement was taken because of changes in Maltese financial laws, and that more recent tax agreements with other countries included provisions for taxation on U.S. social benefits.

- Former Nationalist government owed Lm2.2 million ($6million) to the church. A church-state agreement signed in 1992 provided that the government would make annual grants to the church to help it meet school running costs. The church gave the state considerable property at reduced prices.
- The General Workers Union has seen a steep rise in membership, which has now reached 48,581. The union is bigger than all the other unions combined.
- Opposition Nationalist Party warns the government not to reduce powers of local councils.
- No assurance that water prices will not be increased. The government has ordered a study of the Water Services Corporation which is in dire financial straits.
